project: Feature Flag Smith Feature Tasks Kanban Enabled Prd
overview: Add an In Focus Kanban lane that groups actively running tasks separately from backlog and completed work so operators can inspect live execution quickly.
goals: Surface all running tasks in a dedicated In Focus lane
Keep task movement between lanes deterministic and status-driven
Improve operator speed for identifying active execution
nonGoals: Changing task execution semantics or scheduler behavior
Introducing new task statuses beyond existing domain values
Redesigning the entire Kanban board UI
successMetrics: Operators can identify all running tasks from one lane without cross-lane scanning
Tasks with running status appear in In Focus within one board refresh cycle
No non-running tasks are displayed in In Focus
openQuestions: Should paused tasks remain in their current lane or move to In Focus?
Should In Focus be ordered by start time, last update, or priority?

stack.framework: Existing Smith console frontend and backend task APIs

routes.name: Tasks Kanban View
routes.purpose: Display tasks grouped by lane including In Focus for active execution

uiNotes: Place In Focus as a first-class lane visible without scrolling on desktop layouts where possible.
Display task cards in In Focus with execution metadata needed for quick inspection.

fields.name: status
fields.note: Existing task execution status used for lane assignment

fields.name: lane
fields.note: Derived lane name for board rendering

importFormat: Canonical Smith PRD JSON consumed from `.agents/tasks/prd.json`.
rules: In Focus lane must include only tasks in active execution states.
Lane assignment must be derived from task status and remain deterministic.
Existing non-running lane behavior must remain unchanged.
All lane transitions must be reflected without manual page reload where current board refresh supports it.

stories.title: Define active status to In Focus lane mapping
stories.description: As an operator, I want a clear status mapping so running tasks are consistently grouped into the In Focus lane.
acceptanceCriteria: Document the set of task statuses considered active execution for Kanban grouping.
Board grouping logic maps each active status to lane `In Focus` and leaves other mappings unchanged.
Example: a task with an active execution status renders in In Focus.
Negative case: a task in a non-active status does not render in In Focus.
Automated tests validate mapping for every known task status.

stories.title: Render In Focus lane on tasks Kanban
stories.description: As an operator, I want a dedicated In Focus lane on the board so I can immediately locate active execution tasks.
acceptanceCriteria: Kanban view shows an `In Focus` lane in the lane set.
Lane displays task cards assigned by status mapping from US-001.
Example: when two tasks are running, both appear in In Focus.
Negative case: when no tasks are active, In Focus renders an empty-state treatment instead of stale cards.
UI test verifies lane presence and card counts for seeded task fixtures.

stories.title: Keep lane membership updated as task status changes
stories.description: As an operator, I want tasks to move into and out of In Focus automatically when statuses change so the board reflects current execution.
acceptanceCriteria: When a task changes from non-active to active, it appears in In Focus on the next supported refresh/update cycle.
When a task leaves active execution, it exits In Focus and appears in the correct target lane.
Example: transitioning `queued` -> `running` moves a card into In Focus.
Negative case: transitioning `running` -> `done` removes the card from In Focus and places it in Done.
Integration tests cover both transition directions.

stories.title: Prioritize inspection metadata in In Focus cards
stories.description: As an operator, I want key execution metadata visible on In Focus cards so I can inspect active work without opening each task.
acceptanceCriteria: In Focus cards display existing execution metadata fields required for quick inspection (for example current step and last update time) when available.
Metadata rendering uses existing task data contracts without requiring new backend fields.
Example: a running task card shows its current step and recency indicator.
Negative case: if metadata is missing, the card renders a safe fallback label and remains readable.
Component test verifies metadata rendering and fallback behavior.

stories.title: Validate no regression to existing non-active lanes
stories.description: As an operator, I want existing lane behavior preserved so adding In Focus does not break grouping for backlog, blocked, or completed tasks.
acceptanceCriteria: Non-active statuses continue to appear in their pre-existing lanes with unchanged counts for the same fixture set.
Adding In Focus does not duplicate cards across lanes.
Example: a completed task appears only in Done and never in In Focus.
Negative case: regression test fails if any non-active status is remapped unexpectedly.
Regression suite covers lane counts and exclusivity across all lanes.
